rationale: 13 patch findings: Tauri cmdlog Mutex lacks poison recovery, raw_output is unbounded, ANSI strip misses DEC-private sequences, in-flight records render null exit codes and trigger spurious mapFailure messages, clipboard fallback uses wrong Tauri v2 plugin namespace, write errors are swallowed, PTY tail-output races with close, runStream appends without ANSI stripping, and initCmdLog/copy-all integration lack tests. Commit-format standard fails on 6 commits: 4 use prohibited scope syntax, 2 use bare ticket-key prefix. 2 deferred (pre-existing PTY singleton and kill-sentinel; see code-review-deferred.md); 4 dismissed.

findings.title: Unbounded raw_output growth per record
findings.problem: CmdLogStore.append() has no cap on raw_output length; every chunk extends the String with no size limit or trim.
findings.impact: A verbose or long-running PTY or runStream command fills raw_output without bound for the app session lifetime; on a build or install script this can exhaust heap and OOM the Tauri process.
findings.recommendation: Add a MAX_OUTPUT constant (e.g. 1 MB) and in append() either reject chunks that would exceed it or trim the head: if record.raw_output.len() + chunk.len() > MAX_OUTPUT { record.raw_output = record.raw_output.split_off(chunk.len()); }

findings.title: Poisoned Mutex panics all cmdlog commands
findings.problem: All five cmdlog Tauri commands call state.cmdlog.lock().unwrap(). A panic in any code path that holds the Mutex poisons it; every subsequent cmdlog call then also panics.
findings.impact: If any thread panics while holding the cmdlog lock, the entire cmdlog subsystem becomes permanently unavailable for the session, crashing each IPC handler that calls a cmdlog command.
findings.recommendation: Use state.cmdlog.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) to recover from a poisoned lock, or map the poison error to CmdResult::Err and return it to the frontend.

findings.title: DEC-private CSI sequences not stripped
findings.problem: The ANSI regex alternation \[[0-9;]*[A-Za-z] does not match DEC-private CSI sequences such as \x1b[?25h, \x1b[>0c, or \x1b[!p because the intermediate characters ?/>/ precede the numeric parameters.
findings.impact: DEC-private escape sequences emitted by interactive PTY applications (cursor-hide, mode-set, terminal-attribute queries) survive into cmdlog raw_output and copy-all text, corrupting the log and potentially interfering with mapFailure pattern matching.
findings.recommendation: Extend the CSI alternation: change \[[0-9;]*[A-Za-z] to \[[?!>]?[0-9;:]*[A-Za-z] to cover the standard set of DEC-private intermediate characters.

findings.title: mapFailure returns spurious message for in-flight records
findings.problem: mapFailure checks exit_code === 0 to return early; when exit_code is null (record still open) that check is false and the function continues. If raw_output is empty it returns 'Command exited with code null and produced no output.'; if partial output matches a network or not-found pattern it returns a spurious failure message.
findings.impact: Every in-flight command rendered while running shows a misleading failure message in the UI (cmdlog-ui.js:25) and may include it in the copy-all text (cmdlog-ui.js:47), confusing users before the command finishes.
findings.recommendation: Add a null-guard at the top of mapFailure: if (exit_code === null) return ''; and guard both call sites in cmdlog-ui.js before invoking mapFailure on a record with null exit_code.

findings.title: In-flight records render 'exit null · 0.0s'
findings.problem: meta.textContent = `exit ${r.exit_code} · ${(r.duration_ms / 1000).toFixed(1)}s` runs unconditionally; when a command is still running exit_code is null and duration_ms is null, producing the string 'exit null · 0.0s'.
findings.impact: Every open command entry displays a misleading completion status while still running; on a live build the panel shows false data throughout the command's lifetime.
findings.recommendation: Guard the meta text: meta.textContent = r.exit_code != null ? `exit ${r.exit_code} · ${(r.duration_ms/1000).toFixed(1)}s` : 'running…';

findings.title: No tests for initCmdLog DOM wiring
findings.problem: initCmdLog() has no test coverage; it removes the hidden class, injects the copy button, and wires the toggle listener. Any regression in DOM element IDs, class names, or wiring logic is invisible to the test suite.
findings.impact: If initCmdLog fails silently (wrong element ID, thrown error, missed classList call), the entire command-log panel stays hidden and no records appear at runtime; cmdlog-failure-map.test.mjs and all bridge tests continue to pass regardless.
findings.recommendation: Add ui/test/cmdlog-ui.test.mjs using the DOM-stub pattern from steps-ui.test.mjs; minimally assert that initCmdLog() removes 'hidden' from #command-log-footer and appends a button with id='cmdlog-copy-all' to summary.

findings.title: Copy-all click handler integration untested
findings.problem: The copy-all click handler composes text from _records via mapFailure and calls navigator.clipboard.writeText; no test exercises this path: if mapFailure(r) were replaced by mapFailure(r.id) or the join separator changed, the bug would be undetectable.
findings.impact: Regressions in the copy-all composition (wrong field, wrong separator, missing filter) ship silently; cmdlog-failure-map.test.mjs calls mapFailure directly and cannot catch integration errors in the click handler.
findings.recommendation: In ui/test/cmdlog-ui.test.mjs, stub cmdlog.list, call _renderRecords, simulate a click on #cmdlog-copy-all, and assert that navigator.clipboard.writeText received the expected formatted string.

findings.title: Clipboard write failure silently discarded
findings.problem: Neither navigator.clipboard.writeText(text) (line 50) nor the Tauri fallback writeText (line 52) has a .catch() handler; promise rejections (permission denied, API unavailable) are swallowed with no user feedback.
findings.impact: On clipboard permission denial or API failure the user sees no error; the copy button appears to work but nothing is placed on the clipboard.
findings.recommendation: Attach a .catch() to both branches, e.g. navigator.clipboard.writeText(text).catch(() => { /* show toast or console.warn */ }); and same for the Tauri fallback path.

findings.title: Tauri clipboard fallback uses wrong plugin namespace
findings.problem: window.__TAURI__.clipboardManager.writeText(text) uses camelCase; the Tauri v2 plugin registers under the hyphenated key window.__TAURI__['clipboard-manager'], so clipboardManager is undefined at runtime.
findings.impact: In any context where the secure-context branch does not execute (non-secure context, navigator.clipboard absent), the fallback throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined, and copy silently fails with an unhandled rejection.
findings.recommendation: Replace with window.__TAURI__['clipboard-manager'].writeText(text) or import writeText from the plugin's JS module (@tauri-apps/plugin-clipboard-manager).

findings.title: runStream appends raw text without ANSI stripping
findings.problem: runStream appends p.text from engine:cmd-line events directly to cmdlog with no call to stripAnsi; the PTY path applies stripAnsi but the runStream path does not. Reachability uncertain: depends on whether the Rust run_stream emits ANSI-coloured output.
findings.impact: If a command run via runStream emits ANSI colour codes, those sequences land in raw_output, potentially corrupting mapFailure pattern matches and surfacing escape codes verbatim in the copy-all text.
findings.recommendation: Import and apply stripAnsi to p.text before appending: if (logId) pendingAppends.push(cmdlog.append(logId, stripAnsi(p.text)).catch(console.warn));

findings.title: PTY data appends not awaited before cmdlog.close
findings.problem: In spawnPty, cmdlog.append calls inside the engine:pty-data listener are fire-and-forget (not tracked in an array); the finally block calls cmdlog.close before all in-flight appends have resolved.
findings.impact: The Rust append function rejects calls on an already-closed record; tail output from the final PTY data events races with close and is silently dropped when close wins, producing truncated raw_output for any command whose final output arrives after process exit.
findings.recommendation: Mirror the pendingAppends pattern already used in runStream: push each cmdlog.append(...) promise into an array inside the pty-data listener, and await Promise.all(pendingAppends) in the finally block before calling cmdlog.close.

findings.title: Bare ticket-key commit prefix missing type
findings.problem: Commits 'epmcdme-15231: add planning artifacts' and 'epmcdme-15230: add planning artifacts' use a bare Jira key as the prefix; git-workflow.md requires a recognized type token (feat|fix|docs|test|chore|refactor) as the first segment.
findings.impact: These commits do not conform to the project's documented commit-format standard, which is blocking; automated tooling that parses commit messages (changelog, release notes, CI gates) may reject or misclassify them.
findings.recommendation: Reword to 'chore: add planning artifacts for epmcdme-15231' (and similarly for epmcdme-15230).

findings.title: Commit scope syntax prohibited by git-workflow guide
findings.problem: Four commits use 'feat(EPMCDME-15232): <description>' scope syntax, which git-workflow.md explicitly marks as anti-pattern, preferring 'feat: <description>' with no scope.
findings.impact: Non-conforming commits break the documented commit-format standard, which is listed as blocking in the standards audit; 4 of 16 commits in the branch do not conform.
findings.recommendation: Reword to drop the scope, e.g. 'feat: add cmdlog-ui rendering module and wire into boot' (and similarly for the three other scoped commits).
